title: Llamafile: bringing AI to the masses with fast CPU inference: Stephen Hood and Justine Tunney
talk_summary: Mozilla's Llamafile packages model weights into a single portable executable and optimizes CPU inference (outer-loop unrolling for matmul, lockstep/thread-sync tricks, tinyBLAS) to get 30-500% CPU speedups. The talk is mostly about local/edge inference portability and performance, not agent orchestration or review quality.

takeaways.technique: Cheap CPU/RAM inference for heavy or bulk jobs
takeaways.what_they_do: They run large models on commodity CPUs with lots of cheap RAM instead of GPUs, accepting slower tokens for more intelligence per dollar.
takeaways.evidence_quote: with CPUs for the price of a graphics card I put 512 gigs in my workstation and that means I can run all the frontier models
takeaways.numbers: 512 GB RAM workstation; 30-500% CPU speedups; 22B model on a $350 CPU

takeaways.what_they_do: Weights are bundled into one executable that runs on any OS/CPU/GPU without install, collapsing the local inference stack to one action.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a llama file is a single file executable that runs without any installation on pretty much every operating system

takeaways.technique: CPU tier as overflow when quota is exhausted
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue CPUs are an underused planet-scale resource and can serve inference when GPUs are scarce/expensive.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have an entire planet of CPUs out there literally all over the world great Hardware often affordable hardware
